assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: @TableTest('''...''')' appears twice in the class

assertions.text: Email validation and name-required error scenarios are present
assertions.evidence: Rows: 'Null name' and 'Missing @ in email' cover both required-name and invalid-email

assertions.text: Dietary requirements/accessibility needs use blank cells when absent
assertions.evidence: service.register(..., null, null, ...) passes null for optional fields

assertions.text: Irrelevant inputs use value sets, not blanks
assertions.evidence: In pricing table, name and email are fixed strings; in validation, groupSize=1 is fixed

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as leftmost
assertions.evidence: First column in both tables is 'Scenario'

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?'
assertions.evidence: 'Accepted?', 'Price?', 'Error?' columns present

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language
assertions.evidence: 'Name', 'Email', 'Registration date', 'Group size', 'Price?' are business terms

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions, not outcomes
assertions.evidence: 'Early-bird only', 'Group of 5', 'Missing @' describe input conditions

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: Both test methods contain only assertThat calls; no if/switch in test bodies

assertions.text: Annotations appear in correct order
assertions.evidence: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest appear in that order for both methods

assertions.text: Test method has descriptive title via annotation or name
assertions.evidence: @DisplayName('Input validation') and @DisplayName('Registration pricing')

assertions.text: Multi-line @Description uses text block (triple-quoted), not concatenation
assertions.evidence: @Description('''...multi-line...''') uses triple quotes, not concatenation

assertions.text: Multiple tables address distinct concerns
assertions.evidence: Two separate @TableTest methods: validation (name/email) and pricing (discounts)

assertions.text: Each table has only rows needed for its concern
assertions.evidence: Validation has 6 rows covering name/email rules; pricing has 6 rows for discount rules

assertions.text: Validation and pricing are in separate @TableTest methods
assertions.evidence: validates_name_and_email() and prices_registration() are separate methods

assertions.text: Validation includes optional-field columns with null and non-null values
assertions.evidence: Validation table has no columns for dietaryRequirements or accessibilityNeeds; they are fixed in @Description instead

assertions.text: Registration date uses descriptive values with @TypeConverter
assertions.evidence: 'before cutoff', 'on cutoff', 'after cutoff' with parseRegistrationDate @TypeConverter

assertions.text: Cutoff date visible if using literal dates; passes if descriptive
assertions.evidence: Descriptive dates used, so no literal dates to require a cutoff column

assertions.text: @Description does not duplicate information visible in table
assertions.evidence: Pricing @Description states 'name = ...Alice Smith, email = alice@example.com' which are fixed inputs already implicit from test

assertions.text: Output is 'Discount?' not 'Price?', or both 'Base price' and 'Price?'
assertions.evidence: Uses 'Price?' column without 'Base price' column; discount column would be clearer

assertions.text: Each method has uniform single assertion pattern across rows
assertions.evidence: Validation: assertThat(accepted) + conditional error check; Pricing: two uniform assertions (isAccepted + getPrice)

assertions.text: Optional-fields table includes expected output column
assertions.evidence: No dedicated optional-fields table exists; optional fields not tested with acceptance column

assertions.text: Scenario descriptions avoid redundant field values visible in columns
assertions.evidence: Pricing @Description includes 'name = Alice Smith, email = alice@example.com' which repeat fixed inputs
